sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering chemical reactions that produce large excesses of one chiral form of a molecule. Kagan showed that a chiral catalyst could drive reactions favoring a single chirality. Soai found reactions where a product acted as a catalyst to boost the same reaction, turning a tiny initial excess into over 99 percent of a single form.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Life relies on molecules with specific handedness, or chirality, and key enzymes fail to work with the wrong form. Finding new ways to catalyze specific chiral forms helps address challenges in origin-of-life research. It also has immense practical utility for producing pharmaceuticals, as wrong chiral forms in drugs can be inactive or harmful.

Challenges remain as the party still trails behind Reform UK and Labour in polls.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Senior figures and leader Kemi Badenoch talked about winning the next general election outright at the Conservative gathering in Birmingham. Badenoch has seen her approval rating soar, while the party has seen off the threat from Reform UK for now.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Despite trailing Labour and Reform UK in the polls, the Tories believe improved personal ratings for their leader and the party being viewed as the least hated could help them benefit from tactical voting.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The party is preparing for an election and focusing on the economy, aiming to become one of the top two parties so that anti-Labour voters return to them.
